LLMs are good and bad seemingly at random, but if you can predict where they will do well or badly ahead of time, you can get enormous value from them.

articles.headline: Programming and fatigue

AI is taking over the repetitive and obvious parts of the job, leaving developers to deal with higher-judgment tasks. It is no surprise that these would be more tiring.

articles.headline: AI Is Causing Signal Collapse Everywhere All at Once
articles.blurb: AI is making it increasingly hard to tell good work from bad work and fakes. Humans rely on shortcuts based on signals to make decisions all the time. AI widely undermines these signals and lowers the incentive to produce good work. The speed and scale of the current signal collapse is unprecedented. We need signals to survive in the modern world, and the rapid collapse of many previously dependable signals will create large shifts in society.

articles.headline: The Jevons paradox has a second half

The developer jobs that grow will be the ones that the machines made faster. The demand for software can be bottomless and the work can still move somewhere else.

articles.headline: Safe and Efficient Multi-Epoch Embedding Training
articles.blurb: Pinterest found that training its large ID embeddings for multiple epochs degraded Homefeed ranking quality by nearly 6%. Decoupling embedding optimization from the rest of the model, freezing embeddings during the first epoch, and adapting them later reversed the problem, improving online saves by 1.09%. Semi-synchronous prefetching and communication optimizations also reduced GPU idle time during distributed training.

Rather than build its own engine, the DataGrip team chose DuckDB over Apache Calcite because it was the simplest to integrate. Custom table functions plug DuckDB into DataGrip's existing query execution, so PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MongoDB data can meet in one query.

articles.headline: How Klaviyo Scaled Analytics by Getting Out of the Way

Its KBI system combines over 100 dbt semantic metrics, a curated 90-table environment, and trusted SQL checks behind a common agent interface. Most warehouse queries now originate from agents, reducing dependence on manual analyst requests while keeping data definitions consistent.

articles.headline: The Human Side of the Semantic Layer: Translating Data Meaning Across Teams
articles.blurb: Semantic layers need shared human understanding, because teams can interpret the same metric differently even when its calculation is consistent. Governance should pair formal definitions with plain-language explanations, realistic examples, and clear decision rights, then test whether teams apply them consistently.

articles.headline: The Data Product Platform Navigator

Tom De Wolf proposes a four-level maturity model for self-service data platforms, from fragmented scripts and tickets to integrated developer ecosystems. He argues that Level 3, where complete data products can be provisioned through a platform-as-a-product experience, is the minimum required for scalable decentralized ownership.

articles.headline: Your LLM Writes Good SQL. That's Not the Same as Safe SQL
articles.blurb: Accurate text-to-SQL can still expose unauthorized data when generated queries ignore business context and access policies. In a synthetic benchmark of 900 queries, policy-aware validation applied row filters, column masking, and scope restrictions before execution, eliminating observed data leaks while adding approximately 6.5 ms per query. Permissions must be enforced in code rather than entrusted to model prompts.

articles.headline: Apache Spark 4.3.0 Release
articles.blurb: Apache Spark 4.3.0 brings stateful processing to Structured Streaming's Real-Time Mode, supporting aggregations, deduplication, and custom stateful operations with approximately 100 ms end-to-end latency. Declarative Pipelines adds SCD Type 2 Auto CDC, while the SQL engine gains ASOF joins, JSON_TABLE, and optimizations for smaller workloads.

articles.headline: Apache Hop 2.20 Adds Native Iceberg Pipelines and AI Processing
articles.blurb: Apache Hop 2.20 introduces native Apache Iceberg reads and writes without Spark, partitioned Parquet output, and new data-quality transformations. The open-source ETL platform also adds text embedding pipelines, pgvector integration, OpenLineage support, and an optional AI assistant with human-reviewed changes.

articles.headline: Siglake: An Open-Source Observability Lakehouse Built on Iceberg and DataFusion (GitHub Repo)
articles.blurb: Siglake is a Rust-based observability engine that ingests OpenTelemetry logs and traces into Apache Parquet and Iceberg tables on object storage. Its architecture uses an Arrow write-ahead log for streaming ingestion and DataFusion for distributed SQL queries, eliminating the need for Kafka or proprietary storage formats. The project reports ingesting over 400,000 rows per second in distributed tests.

articles.headline: Cleaning or Recalling? Knowledge Dependence in LLM-based Data Cleaning
articles.blurb: Across eight LLMs, researchers found that data-cleaning performance often depends on familiar names and facts, with one model's year-repair accuracy falling from 91% to 18% when films were renamed. Models also overwrote valid table values with remembered facts, while flawed benchmark answers sometimes rewarded incorrect repairs.

articles.headline: How We Built NASA's Zero-Shot Detector for Gas Leaks from Space
articles.blurb: NASA JPL's Daily Methane Digest scans every scene from the EMIT instrument on the space station and cuts alert times from months to about 24 hours. Its U-Net, trained only on methane, also maps carbon monoxide, ammonia, and nitrogen dioxide plumes without retraining. On two years of archived scenes, it found 157 methane plumes that human review missed.

articles.headline: 91% of Tokenized Stocks Lead Back to One Broker
articles.blurb: The tokenized stocks market has reached $4.60B, but $4.17B (91%) is backed by shares held at a single US broker, Alpaca Securities, used by seven issuers including Binance bStocks, Ondo, Robinhood, and Coinbase. Those shares sit at DTC under Cede & Co., not under the names of the 4.7M token holders spread across those products. Securitize and Backpack route through RQD Clearing but still terminate at DTC, while only Superstate and Securitize's ISTs hold shares on the issuer's own register, removing both a broker and the depository from the chain. An Alpaca insolvency or regulatory action would put 91% of tokenized equity supply and all 4.7M affected holders at risk from a single counterparty event.

articles.headline: Coinbase CEO Backs Tokenizing COIN Stock as Companies Resist
articles.blurb: Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong backed tokenizing Coinbase shares on X, arguing that restricting new shareholder categories harms the business and that companies should serve customers on the platforms they use. His position contrasts with resistance from 67 companies, including Apple, Tesla, Nvidia, and Meta, that have objected to their shares trading on OKXICE, a joint venture between OKX and Intercontinental Exchange. The objectors represent 56 of OKXICE's 62 original target companies, a 90.3% rejection rate. For tokenized equity platforms, the OKXICE data shows that corporate buy-in, not technical infrastructure, is the binding constraint on stock listings.

articles.headline: Tempo launches credit, matching businesses with outside lenders
articles.blurb: Tempo, a payments chain incubated by Stripe and Paradigm, now connects businesses with outside lenders, with draws and repayments settling in stablecoins in under a second, 24/7. Fintechs can borrow for prefunding payouts, receivables, working capital, and consumer credit through a licensed partner. Facilities can have no minimum draw, draws can land as dollars in a bank account and be repaid by wire, and the lender sets terms and takes the risk, not Tempo. articles.headline: A New Market Rate for Liquidity: Aerodrome

Aerodrome breaks this ceiling by paying LPs in AERO, a token that, when staked, earns a share of total network revenue including dynamic fee premiums, liquidity payments, and MEV capture, so staked AERO yields can exceed any single pool's point-in-time fee output. The token capitalizes claims on future network productivity rather than a fixed fee split, so the protocol can subsidize current liquidity costs at a flexible multiplier as the network grows.
